summary.text: This investigation aims to use numerical simulation to explore how gravity influences pyrolysis smoke growth, simulating dibutyl-phthalate (DBP) particles in Earth gravity and microgravity.

geometry.text: Geometry is similar to that considered in the SAME experiments.

flow.text: Two cross-flow velocities were considered, low enough that buoyancy cannot be neglected in the presence of gravity.

gravity.text: Earth gravity and microgravity were simulated.

claims.text: The investigation aims to use numerical simulation to explore the influence of gravity on pyrolysis smoke growth.
The investigation proposes that without buoyancy, mixing and heat transfer are reduced.
The metadata states that models and tools characterizing smoke particles could lead to better smoke detection devices and help prevent fires (stated as a research impact, not as a result).

limitations.text: The work is a numerical simulation study; the metadata describes the simulations but states no simulation result.
This draft cites PSI metadata; no PDF text or experimental-table passages were processed for this investigation.

modeling_resources.description: Simulation output files comparing Earth-gravity and microgravity particle size distributions and number density. No model validation is claimed.

evidence.excerpt: to use numerical simulation to explore the influence of gravity on pyrolysis smoke growth from a fundamental perspective
The formation and growth of dibutyl-phthalate (DBP) particles in Earth gravity and microgravity environments was simulated.
Without buoyancy, mixing and heat transfer are reduced
This would directly lead to better smoke detection devices and prevent fires
This study considered two cross-flow velocities of sufficiently low speed that buoyancy cannot be neglected in the presence of gravity.
